en.title: In Thy Service Will I Ever
en.author: Philipp Spitta
stanzas:
[G]In thy service [C]will I [D]ever,
[G]Jesus, my Re[D7]deemer, [G]stay;
[G]nothing me from [C]thee shall [D]sever,
[G]gladly would I [D7]go the [G]way.
[C]Life in me thy [G]life pro[D]duces,
[Em]and gives vigour [A7]to my [D]heart,
[G]as the vine doth [C]living [D]juices
[G]to the purple [D7]grape im[G]part.

Could I be in other places
half so happy as with thee,
who so many gifts and graces
hast thyself prepared for me?
No place could be half so fitted
to impart true joy, I ween,
since to thee, O Lord, committed
power in heaven and earth hath been.

Where shall I find such a Master,
who hath done my soul such good,
and retrieved the great disaster
sin first caused, by his own blood?
Is not he my rightful owner,
who for me his own life gave?
Were it not a foul dishonour
not to love him to the grave?

Yes, Lord Jesus, I am ever
thine in sorrow and in joy;
death the union shall not sever,
nor eternity destroy.
I am waiting, yea, am sighing
for my summons to depart;
he is best prepared for dying
who in life is thine in heart.

Let thy light on me be shining
when the day is almost gone,
when the evening is declining,
and the night is drawing on;
bless me, O my Father, laying
both thy hands on my meek head,
"Here thy day is ended," saying,
"yonder live the faithful dead."

Stay beside me, when the stillness
and the icy touch of death
fill my trembling soul with chillness,
like the morning's frosty breath;
as my failing eyes grow dimmer,
let my spirit grow more bright,
as I see the first faint glimmer
of the everlasting light.

de.title: Bei dir, Jesu, will ich bleiben
de.author: Philipp Spitta
stanzas:
[G]Bei dir, Jesu, [C]will ich [D]bleiben,
[G]stets in deinem [D7]Dienste [G]stehn;
[G]nichts soll mich von [C]dir ver[D]treiben,
[G]will auf deinen [D7]Wegen [G]gehn.
[C]Du bist meines [G]Lebens [D]Leben,
[Em]meiner Seele [A7]Trieb und [D]Kraft,
[G]wie der Weinstock [C]seinen [D]Reben
[G]zuströmt Kraft und [D7]Lebens[G]saft.

Könnt ich's irgend besser haben
als bei dir, der allezeit
soviel tausend Gnadengaben
für mich Armen hat bereit?
Könnt ich je getroster werden
als bei dir, Herr Jesu Christ,
dem im Himmel und auf Erden
alle Macht gegeben ist?

Wo ist solch ein Herr zu finden,
der, was Jesus tat, mir tut:
mich erkauft von Tod und Sünden
mit dem eignen teuren Blut?
Sollt ich dem nicht angehören,
der sein Leben für mich gab,
sollt ich ihm nicht Treue schwören,
Treue bis in Tod und Grab?

Ja, Herr Jesu, bei dir bleib ich
so in Freude wie in Leid;
bei dir bleib ich, dir verschreib ich
mich für Zeit und Ewigkeit.
Deines Winks bin ich gewärtig,
auch des Rufs aus dieser Welt;
denn der ist zum Sterben fertig,
der sich lebend zu dir hält.

Bleib mir nah auf dieser Erden,
bleib auch, wenn mein Tag sich neigt,
wenn es nun will Abend werden
und die Nacht herniedersteigt.
Lege segnend dann die Hände
mir aufs müde, schwache Haupt,
sprich: "Mein Kind, hier geht's zu Ende;
aber dort lebt, wer hier glaubt."

Bleib mir dann zur Seite stehen,
graut mir vor dem kalten Tod
als dem kühlen, scharfen Wehen
vor dem Himmelsmorgenrot.
Wird mein Auge dunkler, trüber,
dann erleuchte meinen Geist,
dass ich fröhlich zieh hinüber,
wie man nach der Heimat reist.

notes: German is the six-stanza text as evangeliums.net prints it (EG 406), in modern sung orthography — 'tat/tut/teuren' where Spitta's 1833 Psalter und Harfe had 'that/thut/theuren'. Stanza 1 line 1 reads 'Bei dir, Jesu' here, not evangeliums.net's 'Bei dir, Jesus': the EG reading is 'Jesu', which is also the hymn's title on that same page and what the Grosshartmannsdorf EG-406 order of service prints. That order of service is the independent witness for the text — it carries stanzas 1, 2 and 4 (it is a selection, not an abridgement of the hymn) and matches this file word for word across all three, including 'soviel tausend Gnadengaben' and stanza 4's 'Deines Winks bin ich gewärtig'. English is Richard Massie's translation from Lyra Domestica I (1863), 59–60, which renders all six stanzas in the same metre; Massie died in 1887, so it is public domain. Hymnary lists three other 19th-century translations (Walter 1868, Burns 1869, Durand 1873); Massie's is the one that actually reached hymnals (Schaff's Christ in Song 1879, Horder's Congregational Hymns 1884), and it is the only complete one. Tune: the hymn has no melody of its own and is sung to the Herrnhut tune of 'Herz und Herz vereint zusammen' — hymnary names that tune O DU LIEBE MEINER LIEBE, meter 8.7.8.7 D, originally the folk song 'Sollen nun die grünen Jahre' (ca. 1700). CHART CAVEAT: the only score I could source is Lift Up Your Hearts 727, whose scan shows just the first two lines — in G, 4/4, which is why the key needs no transposing under the guitar rule. Lines 1–2 are harmonised from that scan; lines 3–4 and 7–8 reuse them because the tune is documented (hymnary) as rounded bar form AABA. Lines 5–6, the B section, are the guessed part: I took the chords from a spectral analysis of the LUYH 727 recording, which shows the middle of the tune leaving G for the dominant via A7→D before returning, and wrote the plainest reading of that (C–G–D / Em–A7–D). A player with the full score should check those two lines. Both languages' charts agree bar for bar: G on syllable 1, the second change on syllable 5, the third on syllable 7, in every line.
